clinicalPearls: Most severe autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis, caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in ABCA12, a lipid transporter essential for lamellar granule function
Neonates are encased in thick, plate-like armoured scale separated by deep erythematous fissures
Severe ectropion, eclabium, flattened ears, and constricting bands on digits are characteristic
The rigid encasing membrane restricts chest expansion and feeding and predisposes to constriction ischaemia of extremities
Barrier failure causes profound transepidermal water loss, hypernatraemic dehydration, temperature instability, and high infection risk
Early systemic retinoid therapy has substantially improved survival when combined with intensive neonatal supportive care
Survivors typically transition to a severe erythrodermic ichthyosis phenotype resembling congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
reference.pathophysiology: Harlequin ichthyosis is caused by loss of function of ABCA12, an ATP-binding cassette transporter that loads lipids into lamellar granules within keratinocytes. Without functional ABCA12, lipids cannot be delivered to the extracellular space of the stratum corneum, so the lamellar lipid bilayers that normally provide the epidermal permeability barrier fail to form. The result is grossly abnormal cornification with massive hyperkeratosis, a rigid non-pliable scale, and a catastrophically leaky barrier. This produces extreme transepidermal water loss and impaired thermoregulation and defence against infection from birth.
additionalDifferentials: Lamellar ichthyosis / congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma (collodion presentations)
Severe Netherton syndrome in the neonate
additionalInvestigations: ABCA12 molecular genetic testing to confirm diagnosis
Serum electrolytes and close monitoring of fluid balance
Skin biopsy showing massive compact orthohyperkeratosis with electron microscopy showing absent or abnormal lamellar granules
Ophthalmology assessment for ectropion and corneal exposure
Sepsis screen and cultures for suspected infection
Prenatal genetic diagnosis or fetal ultrasound in at-risk pregnancies
redFlags: Respiratory compromise from restricted chest wall movement
Digital or limb ischaemia from constricting bands
reference.prognosis: Historically usually fatal in the neonatal period, but with modern neonatal intensive care and early systemic retinoid therapy a majority of infants now survive, transitioning to a chronic severe ichthyosis with lifelong skin and ocular problems.
pitfalls: Delaying transfer to neonatal intensive care and delaying consideration of systemic retinoids
Underestimating fluid and electrolyte losses through the defective barrier
Missing digital constriction bands that threaten limb viability
Neglecting corneal protection in the presence of severe ectropion
management: Start early systemic retinoid therapy such as acitretin to soften and shed the armoured scale and improve survival
Nurse in a humidified incubator with meticulous replacement of fluid and electrolytes to counter massive transepidermal water loss and hypernatraemic dehydration
Apply liberal emollients and gentle wound care, watching constricting bands on the digits for ischaemia and releasing them if perfusion is threatened
Prevent and promptly treat sepsis given the failed skin barrier
Provide high-calorie nutritional support for the raised metabolic demand and impaired feeding
Obtain ophthalmology review with lubrication for ectropion and corneal exposure
Coordinate multidisciplinary neonatal intensive care across dermatology, ophthalmology, and clinical genetics
Offer genetic counselling and prenatal diagnosis for future pregnancies given autosomal recessive ABCA12 disease
